cards.text: Moses is still preaching to Israel about life in the land the LORD is giving them. And he opens with a hard one. Someone is found killed, lying in a field, and nobody knows who did it.

cards.question: Nobody knows who killed the man in the field. So who has to come out first?

cards.text: Out comes the measuring, from the body to every town around it. Friend, half the time I can't even land a stamp in the middle of a cookie, and these elders are measuring all the way to whole towns.

cards.question: Why do the elders and judges measure from the body to the towns around it?

answers.text: To mark out a grave site

cards.text: Whichever city comes out closest, the job lands on its elders. And they have to bring an animal.

cards.question: The elders of the nearest city take a ___ that has never been yoked or used for work.

cards.text: They lead the heifer down to a valley with running water. It's ground nobody has ever plowed or planted.

cards.question: In that valley, the elders offer the heifer on an altar as a burnt offering.

cards.text: Instead, they break its neck right there by the stream. Then the priests, the sons of Levi, step forward.

cards.question: Why are the priests, the sons of Levi, part of this?

answers.text: God chose them to serve and rule on cases
They live in the city nearest the field
They were the ones who found the victim

cards.text: Then every elder of the nearest city washes his hands in the stream, right over the heifer.

cards.question: As they wash their hands by the stream, the elders declare that they saw who killed the man.

cards.text: They say their hands didn't shed this blood and their eyes didn't see it. Then they pray, "Accept this atonement, O LORD, for Your people Israel whom You have redeemed, and do not hold the shedding of innocent blood against them."

cards.question: Moses says that after the elders pray, the bloodshed will be atoned for.
With the heifer, the washing and the prayer, Israel purges the ___ of shedding innocent blood from among them.

cards.text: They've done what is right in the eyes of the LORD. Nobody gets to say "not my field, not my problem," because the closest town has to show up.
Moses moves on to war. When the LORD gives Israel's enemies into their hand and they take captives, a man might see a beautiful woman among them and want her as his wife.
He brings her into his house. But Moses lays out steps that come before any marriage.

cards.question: Once the captive woman is in the man's house, what does Moses say she must do?

answers.text: Shave her head and trim her nails
Learn all the laws of Israel
Serve his family as a maid

cards.text: She also puts aside the clothes she was captured in. Then she gets time in his house to mourn her father and mother.

cards.question: The captive woman lives in his house and mourns her father and mother for a full ___ before he can marry her.

cards.text: Then Moses covers what happens if the man isn't pleased with her.

cards.question: If the man isn't pleased with the woman he married, he's allowed to sell her for money.
The man must let her go wherever she wishes and never treat her as a slave. What reason does Moses give?

answers.text: She came from a royal family
Her people might come for her

cards.text: Next, a man has two wives, one loved and one unloved, and both give him sons. The firstborn son is from the unloved wife.

cards.question: When he divides his inheritance, the man can name the loved wife's son as the firstborn instead.

cards.text: No playing favorites with the firstborn. I gave all six of my kids a topping each, because if I EVER picked a favorite, Mags would ring that bell till the oven doors rattled.

cards.question: What must the father give the unloved wife's son, his true firstborn?

answers.text: A double portion of all he has
The family house and the land

cards.question: Why does Moses say the right of the firstborn belongs to the unloved wife's son?

answers.text: He is the firstfruits of his father's strength
His mother was the first wife the man married
He has always been the strongest of the sons

cards.text: Now Moses turns to a heavy one. A son is stubborn and rebellious, and he won't listen to his father and mother, even when they discipline him.

cards.question: The stubborn son's father and mother take hold of him and bring him to the ___ of his city, at the gate of his hometown.

cards.text: At the gate, they tell the elders their son is stubborn and rebellious and won't obey them. Then they add, "He is a glutton and a drunkard."

cards.question: After the parents speak to the elders, what does Moses say happens to the rebellious son?

answers.text: The men of his city stone him
He is sent out of the land
He serves the elders for a year

cards.question: Moses says the rebellious son's case is kept quiet so the rest of Israel never hears about it.

cards.text: Last law in this stretch. A man commits a sin worthy of death, he is executed, and his body is hung on a tree.

cards.question: How long can the executed man's body be left on the tree?

answers.text: He must be buried that day

cards.question: The body can't stay up overnight, because anyone who is hung on a tree is under God's ___.

cards.text: Paul points back to this law later, writing about Jesus. He says Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us (Galatians 3:13).
Moses wraps it up: they must not defile the land the LORD their God is giving them as an inheritance. And friend, this sermon isn't over yet.

rule.text: He calls the baker "baker" or "friend," and talks to one baker at a time. Never "my baker," "kids" or "sweetie."

findings.problem: Moses appears for the first time in this lesson, but the card never says who he is. It only says he is 'still preaching to Israel.'

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The card says 'Then they pray.' Deuteronomy 21:7 says the elders 'shall declare,' and the declaration includes the words addressed to the LORD. Renaming the declaration a prayer matches the Naomi example the rule warns against.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The question says 'after the elders pray.' The text calls what the elders say a declaration (Deuteronomy 21:7), not a prayer.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The question says 'the washing and the prayer.' The text calls what the elders say a declaration (Deuteronomy 21:7), not a prayer.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The card says nobody gets to say 'not my field, not my problem,' because the closest town has to show up. That explains what the law was for, and the text never states that purpose. It also tells content from verses 3 and 6, but the card cites only verse 9.

rule.text: Connecting passages. When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

findings.problem: The joke compares the law to giving each kid one topping so no one is the favorite. That is equal shares. The law is the opposite: the true firstborn must get a double portion (Deuteronomy 21:17), whichever wife is loved. The comparison doesn't share the passage's action and muddies the fact the next card asks about. The opening line 'No playing favorites with the firstborn' also misstates the law, which is about not letting favoritism toward a wife override the firstborn's right.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'He is the firstfruits of his father's strength,' uses Bible wording. The wrong answers are plain modern wording, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Verse 21 says 'So you must purge the evil from among you, and all Israel will hear and be afraid.' No card ever tells this. The true or false card has False as its answer, so the baker only learns that the case isn't kept quiet. They never learn that all Israel will hear and be afraid, or the purge line.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The question asks 'How long,' and the two wrong answers are lengths of time or conditions. The right answer, 'He must be buried that day,' is a command about burial, so it isn't the same kind of thing as the others.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This story card tells only Galatians 3:13. It tells no part of Deuteronomy 21, yet its verses field cites Deuteronomy 21:23. The Galatians connection should ride along on a card that tells the passage.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: Paul appears for the first time in this lesson, but the card never says who he is.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The whole passage is case laws: the unsolved murder, captive wives, the firstborn's inheritance, the rebellious son and the hanged body. That looks like the 'rules for everyday life' stretch, which gets one summary card and no choice cards. But the same rule says 'speeches, teaching and key laws' get full cards, and the passage is a Sermon inside Moses' speech. The walkthrough treats every law in full, with choice cards.
findings.question: When an entire passage is a run of everyday laws inside a speech or sermon, like Deuteronomy 12–26, should it get full story and choice cards, or be handled as a long stretch? Which laws count as 'key laws'?
